paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: The effect of and by language family. Error bars indicate the standard deviation.
model_annotation: This grouped vertical bar chart illustrates the measured "effect" across nine different language families under four distinct model conditions. The horizontal axis displays the categorical language families, which are arranged in alphabetical order from left to right: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis represents the numerical value, labeled as "effect," utilizing a linear scale with tick marks and corresponding horizontal grid lines placed at regular intervals of 10, ranging from 0 to 40. Within each language family category on the horizontal axis, the data is visually arranged into a cluster of four adjoining bars. According to the legend, these bars correspond to the conditions "mBERT-targ" (shaded light blue), "XLM-targ" (shaded dark blue), "mBERT-permute" (shaded light green), and "XLM-permute" (shaded dark green). Every bar features a solid black outline and is visually emphasized with a capped vertical black line representing the standard deviation, some of which extend below the zero baseline. The approximate heights of the bars vary widely across the chart; the tallest individual bar belongs to the mBERT-targ condition in the Isolate category, reaching a value of roughly 35, while the shortest bar is the XLM-permute condition in the Uralic category, displaying a value just above 0. In several language families, such as Isolate and Uralic, the light and dark blue bars visually exceed the green bars, whereas in the IE-Indic category, the green mBERT-permute and XLM-permute bars measure approximately 18 and 16 respectively, surpassing the blue mBERT-targ and XLM-targ bars, which measure roughly 4 and 5.
